Description: Baku's Green Market started origin-labelling dairy in August 2026 (producer; district; phone). Shoppers already buy qatıq, pendir and cream at Taza Bazaar; grocery still under-indexes named village dairy versus Bravo/Araz private label.

Qutab, dolma, plov kits and tandir bread are daily Baku food, not restaurant-only. Delivery grocery can own the weeknight version: washed herbs, grape leaves, chestnuts in season, and ready dough — especially Yasamal students and Nasimi families.

UCB, Fine Cup, 42 Coffee and SENSUM have turned Baku into a roast-at-home market. Landmark and Khalglar (White City) will take whole-bean SKUs; Binagadi will not. List local roasters, not only imported capsules.

Trend: Azerbaijani wine and brandy in grocery
Description: Savalan, Chabiant, Meysari and Goygol are sold in Baku shops but still feel like a restaurant or boutique buy. Landmark and Khalglar can range a short local wine/brandy set instead of only imported New World.

Trend: Caspian smoked fish and caviar grocery formats
Description: Taza Bazaar still holds smoked sturgeon, trout and caviar that supermarket aisles treat as gift-only. A sealed, cold-chain grocery format would serve the original Baku store and Landmark gift baskets without sending customers back to the market.
